title: 講義：インフレの仕組み
lines: A
Inflation is often described as too much money chasing too few goods, but that's only part of the story.
A
Expectations play a surprisingly large role: if people believe prices will rise, they tend to spend sooner and demand higher wages.
A
Businesses, anticipating higher costs, raise their prices in advance, which in turn confirms everyone's expectations.
A
This is why central banks put so much effort into appearing credible, sometimes more than into the interest rate itself.

questions.q: 講師が強調している要因は？
questions.explain: Expectations play a surprisingly large role

questions.q: 中央銀行が信頼性を重視する理由は？
choices: 人々の物価予想に影響を与えるため
法律で決まっているため
questions.explain: 予想が自己実現的に物価を押し上げるので、信頼されることで予想を安定させようとします。

title: パネル討論：AIと仕事
lines: A
Let's turn to the question everyone's asking: will these tools replace jobs or just reshape them?
B
Historically, automation has eliminated specific tasks rather than entire occupations, and I don't see why this time would be fundamentally different.
C
I'd push back on that a little. The pace is what's different. People had decades to adjust before; now it might be a few years.
B
That's fair, though I'd argue the bottleneck is retraining, not the technology itself.
A
So we're agreed that policy has some catching up to do.

choices: 自動化は職業全体を消してきた
自動化は職業全体ではなく特定の作業を消してきた
自動化は雇用を減らさない
questions.explain: eliminated specific tasks rather than entire occupations

questions.q: C が「違う」と言った点は？

title: 歴史ポッドキャスト：時間の標準化
lines: A
It's easy to forget that until the late nineteenth century, almost every town kept its own local time, set by the position of the sun.
A
That worked perfectly well until railways made it possible to cross several of these time zones in a single afternoon.
A
Timetables became a nightmare, and in 1883, the American railroads simply agreed among themselves to adopt standard time zones.
A
Remarkably, it took the federal government another thirty-five years to make it official.

questions.q: 19世紀後半まで各町の時刻はどう決まっていた？
choices: 太陽の位置による地方時
questions.explain: local time, set by the position of the sun

questions.q: 話し手が remarkably と強調したのは？
choices: 政府の公式化が35年も遅れたこと
時刻表がなかったこと
questions.explain: it took the federal government another thirty-five years to make it official

title: 科学ニュース：深海の発見
lines: A
Researchers exploring a deep-sea trench off the coast of Chile have identified what they believe are more than a dozen previously unknown species.
A
Among them is a translucent fish that appears to survive at depths where the pressure would crush most submarines.
A
The team cautioned, however, that confirming the findings will require genetic analysis, which could take up to two years.
A
They also warned that deep-sea mining proposals in the region could threaten these ecosystems before they're properly understood.

questions.q: 発見について研究チームが慎重な理由は？
choices: 確認に最長2年の遺伝子分析が必要
questions.explain: confirming the findings will require genetic analysis, which could take up to two years

title: 読書会
lines: A
I have to admit, I found the ending a bit of a letdown after such a gripping first half.
B
Really? I thought the ambiguity was the whole point. She deliberately leaves it unresolved.
A
Maybe, but it felt less like a choice and more like she'd run out of ideas.
B
I can see why you'd read it that way, but the clues are all there if you go back to the opening chapter.

questions.q: A の結末への評価は？
choices: 前半に比べて期待外れ
questions.explain: a bit of a letdown after such a gripping first half

choices: 作者はアイデアが尽きた
曖昧さは意図的で、冒頭に手がかりがある
questions.explain: the ambiguity was the whole point / the clues are all there

title: 経営戦略の振り返り
lines: A
Looking back, our biggest mistake wasn't entering the European market; it was trying to enter five countries at once.
A
We spread our resources so thin that we couldn't build a meaningful presence anywhere.
A
Had we focused on Germany alone for the first eighteen months, I suspect we'd have been profitable by now.
A
The lesson I'd pass on is that sequencing often matters more than the strategy itself.

choices: 5か国に同時に進出したこと
ドイツに集中したこと
questions.explain: trying to enter five countries at once

choices: 戦略より順序が重要なことが多い
questions.explain: sequencing often matters more than the strategy itself
